spec.title: vscode-extension PROP-002: Configuration, upstream identity and tree layout

status.comment: the type's answers to the identity and layout questions of PROP-016 §2, and the schema of its typeConfig; written 2026-11-01 from DESIGN-002

p.VSX-TYPE-CONFIG: `typeConfig` of a patch set of this type, every path from the tree root, POSIX, without a leading or trailing slash: `ownRoot` (required; PROP-016 `TYPE-OWN-ROOT`), `extensionRoot` (required; the directory whose `package.json` is the extension manifest; `.` for a repository that is one extension), `monorepo` (optional boolean, default false; true when the extension is one workspace package of a larger repository, which adds the root manifest to the fingerprints and a second dependency root), `packageManager` (optional, one of `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`; default `npm`; PROP-004 `VSX-PACKAGE-MANAGER`), `tagPattern` (optional regular expression source; default of `VSX-PIN-TAGS`), `scripts` (optional object: `build`, a script name, default `compile`; `lint`, a list of script names, default `["lint"]`; `test`, `{command, ownGlobArg?}` as the `generic` type takes it, default absent; `package`, a script name of the extension manifest, default absent - PROP-004), `entryModules` (optional list of tree paths, default `["<extensionRoot>/src/extension.ts"]`; PROP-003 `VSX-ENTRY-MODULE`), `localeManifests` (optional list of tree paths of locale manifests the overlay may target; PROP-003 `VSX-LOCALE-MANIFEST-OVERLAYS`), `cleanupWhitelist` and `packageScratch` (optional pattern lists added to the family's), `outputs` (optional pattern list replacing the default of `VSX-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS`), `stamps` (optional list of `{name, value}` literals; PROP-004 `VSX-STAMPS`), `watch` (optional `{channels: [...]}` in the shape of the `generic` type's `commands.compile`, replacing the family's default channels; PROP-004 `VSX-BUILD-CHANNELS`), `preview` (optional `{host?, workspace?}`: an executable path or name the host resolution of `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PREVIEW-HOST` reads third, and a tree-relative or absolute folder the host opens by default), `licensing` (optional `{upstreamLicenceFile?, upstreamComponent?}`: the name of the upstream's licence file in the extension root, default `LICENSE`, and the lower-case component its text ships under, default `upstream`; PROP-006 `VSX-COMPONENT-LICENCES`). Unknown fields are refused, every refusal is `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the field (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONFIG-FIELD`), and `ownRoot` must lie under `<extensionRoot>/src/` (`VSX-OWN-ROOT`).

p.VSX-PIN-TAGS: A pin of this family is an ordinary release tag, `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` or the same without the `v`: the default `tagPattern` is `^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, and a repository with another release train declares its own in `typeConfig.tagPattern`. A tag that moves - `latest`, `nightly`, a channel name - matches neither and is not a pin; the engine resolves the pin to `tag@sha@date` as for every family (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-IDENTITY`).

p.VSX-TREE-FINGERPRINT: What proves that a directory is a tree of this family: `<extensionRoot>/package.json` exists, parses as a JSON object, carries a non-empty `name` and `publisher`, an `engines.vscode` range, and at least one of `main`, `browser` or `contributes` - the manifest of an extension is the one file every extension has and the host refuses to load one without the engine range. With `typeConfig.monorepo` the root `package.json` is a second fingerprint: it must parse as a JSON object that declares `workspaces`, because a package that is not a workspace member is not installed by the root install. A manifest that cannot be parsed is `CK-E-ARTIFACT-BROKEN` naming the file (the `brokenArtifact` of the contract); a manifest that parses and lacks a fingerprint fails `check-tree` with the detail completing `<path>: ...` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-008#ID-CHECK-FINGERPRINTS`).

p.VSX-PACKAGE-MANAGER-FINGERPRINT: When the root manifest declares `packageManager` - `<name>@<version>`, the field npm, pnpm, yarn and bun all honour - its name must be the manager `typeConfig.packageManager` declares; a disagreement fails `check-tree` with both names in the detail, because an install with the wrong manager rewrites the lockfile of the tree. A root manifest without the field proves nothing and the declaration stands.

p.VSX-OWN-ROOT: The own root lies under `<extensionRoot>/src/`: the bundler of the family reaches a module only from the activation entry of the extension, and the type check, the lint and the tests of an extension are anchored at its `src/`. A root outside it is `CK-E-CONFIG` naming the constraint; the field is required and has no default (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-OWN-ROOT`). The engine treats the root as an opaque directory - mirrored by content, excluded from the drift guard, named in the inventory.

p.VSX-ONE-OWNED-DIRECTORY: The type owns exactly one directory, the own root, with no build outputs inside it: the bundler writes outside `src/`, into `dist/` or `out/` of the extension root, so nothing a build writes is ever read as a change of own code (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LAYOUT`).

p.VSX-NO-OWN-EXTENSION-PATH: `ownExtensionPath` answers null: an extension has no extension host of its own into which a second extension could be materialized, and the capability `own-extensions` is absent (PROP-001 `VSX-ABSENCES`).

p.VSX-CLEANUP-WHITELIST: The untracked outputs a fresh pass keeps, the value of `cleanupWhitelist` for this type: `node_modules/` at any depth, `<extensionRoot>/dist/`, `<extensionRoot>/out/`, `<extensionRoot>/*.vsix`, `.vscode-test/` at any depth, `**/.turbo/`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo` at any depth, plus whatever `typeConfig.cleanupWhitelist` adds. Everything else untracked is removed by a fresh pass, under the engine's semantics (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#CLEANUP-WHITELIST-CONTENT`).

p.VSX-FORBIDDEN-TARGETS: The forbidden patch targets of this type: every lockfile of the four package managers (`package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`) at any depth, and the overlay targets of PROP-003. A lockfile is regenerated by the install and a patch of it is overwritten by the next install; the field, its additive extension and the refusal `CK-E-FORBIDDEN-TARGET` are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-003#CONV-FORBIDDEN-TARGETS`).
